subject: Globex RFP: SLO validation methodology and service credit calculation
messages:
From: Alicia Mendes <procurement@globex.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bauer <legal@globex.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for clarification: SLA measurement methodology (Redwood RFP)

Vanessa,

Thanks for the RFP response packet — the team ran the SLA section in our template and has a few follow-ups to help our SRE and procurement teams sign off. Key asks below; we've pulled them from the questionnaire to make it easier to map to your materials.

1) Uptime definition: please confirm the exact service boundary for "availability" used to compute company uptime. Is it "API gateway + inference runtime" or a narrower proxy? Does it exclude scheduled maintenance windows?

2) Latency SLOs: do you measure at p50/p95/p99 end-to-end from client TCP to token delivered, or do you publish internal service-side percentiles? Which measurement agents and time windows are used (e.g., rolling 24h, 30d)?

3) Sampling & telemetry: if we provision dedicated capacity, what sampling rate for request tracing/latency is applied by default, and can we request full tracing for particular routes? How long are raw telemetry logs retained?

4) Service credit calculation: provide the formula you use to convert measured downtime / latency breaches into credits. Include examples for a monthly bill of $100k.

5) Dispute resolution: what evidence will you provide for measurement disputes (telemetry exports, sample traces, raw logs)? SLA evidence/export format?

We'd like to get written answers so our legal and SRE teams can reconcile with our template. If attachments or a short call would help, we can do that next week.

Thanks,
Alicia Mendes
Senior Procurement Manager
Globex Corporation

--

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for clarification: SLA measurement methodology (Redwood RFP)

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. I've consolidated answers below and attached a brief appendix that shows measurement examples and the credit formula. Where helpful I noted follow-ups for engineering/legal. If you'd like, we can run a 30-minute walkthrough early next week.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Availability boundary: "API edge + serving runtime" (requests are considered successful when the API returns a 2xx and the service-side generation completes). Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded when announced with >=72 hours notice; emergency maintenance is handled per our incident escalation process and is only excluded if declared per the Maintenance policy in section 2 of the appendix.
- Latency measurement: we publish service-side percentiles measured at the inference gateway for end-to-end request-to-first-token and request-to-last-token (p50/p95/p99) on a rolling 30d window by default. Customer-configurable dashboards can sample at higher resolution for Dedicated customers.
- Sampling & telemetry: default sampling for request traces is 1% across hosted tenants; Dedicated customers get 100% request metadata (no full payload capture by default). Raw telemetry logs retained for 90 days; aggregated SLO artifacts retained for 24 months.
- Credit calculation: monthly credit = (downtime_minutes / total_month_minutes) * monthly_service_fee * credit_multiplier. Appendix includes worked examples for $100k monthly.
- Evidence: upon dispute we provide the telemetry export (CSV) with timestamps, request ids, and sampled traces; we also provide a signed measurement summary and a time-series export from our observability backend.

I've attached: Redwood_SLA_Measurement_Appendix_v1.pdf (measurement definitions, examples, credit calc) and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) spreadsheet that lists evidence exchange steps.

Notes / follow-ups for your legal team: 1) our maintenance exclusion requires >=72 hours notice for planned updates; 2) credit multiplier caps at 100% of monthly fee for severe outages — further details in the appendix. Tom — happy to flag anything you want us to clarify.

Best,

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the questions and for the patience while we looped in Ops and Legal. Attached is the finalized appendix (Redwood_SLA_Measurement_Appendix_v1.pdf) and the MAP spreadsheet. Highlights of edits we made based on internal review:

- Maintenance: planned maintenance is excluded with >=72 hours notice. For Dedicated on-prem customers we added an on-prem note that customer-managed maintenance windows will be recognized per the deployment agreement (see appendix section 2.3).
- Evidence & dispute timeline: disputes must be raised within 30 days of the affected meter period; we will provide a telemetry export (CSV) and measurement summary within 7 business days of formal request.
- Sampling: default tracing for hosted tenants is 1%; Dedicated customers receive full request metadata exports (no full payload capture by default). We can enable elevated per-route sampling windows (e.g., 7 days) on request subject to resource review; that process is in the MAP.
- Credit calculation: formula and two worked examples included in the appendix; credit cap remains at 100% of monthly service fees per invoice.

Next steps: please confirm if you'd like a short walkthrough (we're available Wed/Thu next week PST) and whether the MAP items align with your SRE's expectations. Once you confirm, we can also push the appendix into the DocuSign envelope for an exhibit attachment if your legal team prefers.
